blockers.title: Eleven decisions waiting on a human
blockers.body: ONE OF THE ELEVEN IS NOW RULED — M6 streak monotonicity, decided wave 13 in favour of the signup-day option; see the M6 card. PROCESS NOTE BEFORE THE LIST, because it changes what these numbers mean. X1 ran ELEVEN rounds, and the piece’s actual bar - the four modes feel like one game - was verified met on every player-reachable route back at round five. Rounds six through eleven were all about the ENUMERATION INSTRUMENT rather than the game, and each one was a real defect found by a real falsifier I ran myself. But while that happened, TWO MERGED PIECES SAT UNGRADED: the cut-in gate, and the app shell whose played-session work found the only real shipped bug of the run. Both are now with critics. The lesson is not that the X1 rounds were wasted - each closed something live - it is that depth on one instrument bought nothing while breadth went unchecked, and nothing in the loop noticed. || Eight decisions are stacked up and none of them are mine to make. In priority order. (1) RECOVERY DAY CONSUMPTION - the only change that closes the streak monotonicity residue, where 37 trained days end on a 37-day streak and 38 end on 18, unbounded. The arm-ahead rework fixed look-dependence completely but not this, and the cause is that idle days before a run are free while idle days inside a live run cost a finite consumable. Closing it means Recovery Days stop being consumed, which touches the hold cap, the earning table and 8.2 - a monetisation decision. MEASURED THIS WAVE rather than argued: an exhaustive probe over 400 seeded 40-day schedules and every single-day superset of each gives 58 violations at today's balance, worst deficit 16 - one schedule ends on 18 and drops to 2 when one more day is trained. With Recovery Days never debited the same probe returns ZERO violations and the named pair inverts the right way ({5,6,7} ends on 3, {0,5,6,7} on 4). So the fix is verified to work; what is left is purely whether you want the economy that comes with it. The obvious alternative - charge the idle days BEFORE a run starts, killing the asymmetry from the other side - needs a new signup-day field on the server-authoritative streak state, so it is not the cheap option it looks like. (1B) THE LIFTER PALETTE BANK IS FULL, AND TWO SEPARATE PIECES HAVE NOW HIT IT. A1’s craft clause fails on floorShare, which is exactly perimeter over area because our skin ramp has four entries and entry 0 is reserved for the contour by construction - no fill pixel can ever land on it. The reference has SIX skin steps and spends 10.4% of its skin on its floor, and floorShare is the only statistic in that comparison that is not ramp-depth-normalised, which is why it is the one that fails. So the reference’s own answer to this clause is a deeper ramp, not a wider limb. B1 hit the same wall from the other side: bank 0 holds only four kit colours, so a partner green or crimson costs a slot. I checked the arithmetic: THE LIFTER BANK IS 16/16 - slot 0 transparent plus outline, four skin steps, SKIN_FLUSH, three singlet, two hair, three gear and CHALK. Two more skin steps means giving up two of those. SKIN_FLUSH, CHALK and the second hair step are the obvious candidates (HAIR already doubles HAIR_DARK, so hair really has two colours, not three). This is a look decision, not a correctness one, so it is yours. Builders are forbidden from taking it. (1C) THE FIGURE READS AS ARMS WITH A TORSO BEHIND THEM. Two critics and I have now independently looked at the 6x frames and read it the same way: upper arm and forearm merge into one lumpy mass per side with no delt-biceps-elbow-forearm structure, the singlet is a narrow blue wedge, and in the hole the kit above the belt is a sliver. In the committed reference the torso is unambiguously the largest single mass with the limbs subordinate to it. OURS INVERTS THAT. At 1x it reads fine - head, blue V of kit, dark belt, sleeves, bar - so this is NOT a phone-scale readability failure, which is the half of 12.2 that is gradeable here. It is a proportion miss against the era bar, and the fix is not a radius tweak: two rounds have now been spent on radii and the second one had to be reverted. It is a question about the whole rig, it is an art judgement, and CLAUDE.md says plainly that a critic cannot settle it on reasoning alone. Builders are fenced off it until you look. (2) POUND MEETS ON THE RESULT CARD - buildResultCard refuses them outright today because every column on that sheet is a kg column. Three options are written into 11: kg-only with lbs as a display skin, pound meets with a unit on the lifter profile, or pound meets shipping without DOTS. It ties into the existing open question about default units. (3) CITATION VERSUS CONTENT - THE COUNT WAS WRONG BY 3.5x AND IS NOW CORRECT. The audit could not see the name this codebase cites most: OpenPowerlifting was absent from the watchlist entirely, and a builder added a fresh mention this wave with the suite staying green. A critic then found a second miss of the same shape - a real fighting-game character named in an art comment - which exposed the real pattern: the watchlist was only ever catching POWERLIFTING names, while a 16-bit pixel-art project cites GAME-INDUSTRY ones constantly, because it reasons about era references in every art file. Corrected: 60 rows / 84 mentions / 18 files became 145 ROWS / 295 MENTIONS / 42 FILES. Split, because these plausibly rule differently: sport-domain meet software 29 rows; game-industry console/franchise/character 23 rows; cited source accounts and apps 15 rows; named comparators 12 rows; a baseball league, club and current player 6 rows; and the original 60. By position: 86 comment, 40 code, 17 prose, 2 filename. Nothing was ruled on - the point was to hand you a real number instead of a wrong one. The audit also had a self-scan widening, now closed and failing-closed: its own exempt window ran to the NEXT declaration, so it swallowed a 20-line doc comment and grew every time somebody wrote a longer paragraph. Nothing was hiding there, but nothing could have been found. (3B) AND ONE ROW IS NOT A SENTENCE, IT IS A PICTURE. docs/reference/sprite-ref-2-16bit-baseball.png contains a real league wordmark, a real club logo and a named currently-competing player - I opened it and confirmed. It is read ONLY by lifterSprite.test.ts as a negative control, it does NOT reach the shipped bundle (app.json points at ./assets/, docs/ is not exported), and both the GitHub repo and the Netlify site are private, which I verified. So the exposure is bounded. But CLAUDE.md names "likeness" explicitly and calls real IP a legal exposure rather than a style preference, and the audit only knows this image exists because somebody transcribed its caption - had nobody written it down, the picture would be exactly as unlicensed and the scan would report nothing. Deleting it costs a real negative control, so it is your call, not mine. (4) THE RPE RUNG DEGENERACY - every rung reports the same e1RM because the chart cancels, so a player optimising should always take the lightest. The identified unbuilt fix is an AMRAP top set, worth +4.7 percent at 100 percent of e1RM using only the published chart, left out because it adds a decision beat and unbounds session length. (5) IS 60 SECONDS A FLOOR AT ALL - measured machine time is 54.3 to 60.3 seconds across the ladder, under 3.2's stated floor, and the guessed pad that used to hide that is gone. If 3.2 means 60 to 90 seconds INCLUDING the player's own reading and tapping there is no divergence at all. (6) TRAINING IQ AND THE PACE VOCABULARY - 8.1 forbids selling training pace, and progression.ts answers can-this-be-bought per fact through a NAME-based floor. trainingIq matches none of those words yet means how well you train and shapes long-run growth. A fact that means pace without naming it is exactly what that floor cannot see. (7) SHEFFIELD - the fictional meet is set in Sheffield, England while the real-IP watchlist carries two real Sheffield meet series, and the result card prints the city on the surface 6.5 calls the strongest organic growth lever. Not a 12.3 violation as written, since a city is not an athlete, brand or company. Worth five seconds. (8) THE FEEL TUNING PASS ITSELF - 12.1 budgets roughly 30 hand iterations after the run, and every walkout duration, judging threshold, crowd rise, haptic pattern and sound recipe is an unplayed placeholder that says so in its own header.
blockers.consequence: None of these block the build - every one is recorded in the GDD or a module header where the code cannot drift from it silently, and each has a stated default the code follows today. They are listed together because they had accumulated across eight rounds of reports and were becoming hard to see. Items 1, 2 and 4 change player-facing behaviour. Item 3 is a legal-adjacent judgement on a list a machine has already assembled. Items 5 through 8 are cheap.

blockers.title: Real-IP is now a refusal condition on EVERY piece, not a gate on one
blockers.body: GDD §12.3 gains two entries: no real named athlete, brand or company identity hardcoded into any asset, string, config or code path; and no branded item with any mechanical effect its fictional equivalent lacks. CLAUDE.md gains the matching hard constraints. GDD §7.3 documents the three-tier identity pattern and §8.1 extends never-sell-power to sponsors, because a paying partner has leverage a player does not.
blockers.consequence: Every critic sweeps it by name from now on, the same way it sweeps the fatigue meter, and the answer must be a statement of what was searched rather than looks fine. The three live builders were messaged mid-flight with the surfaces most at risk in their own piece - equipment marks and gym banners for the environment, the crowd and judge table and ghost lifter names for meet day, and Tier 1 staying generic for the sprite. I also removed three real apparel brands that GDD §8.3A had been naming as candidate partners since before this rule: a document that names candidates while stating the rule is arguing with itself.

blockers.title: Both S1 design questions ruled by the human
blockers.body: Growth coupling: e1rm.ts and its cancellation property are CORRECT and stay untouched — that was never the bug. The gap is that the nudge is a flat constant not coupled to training stimulus, so a primed tap is free and strictly dominant (200kg to 770.65kg over 30 sessions, a PR on 30 of 30). Ruled NOT to fix it now: it belongs to the fatigue/progression module, which does not exist yet, and a stopgap in the daily loop would be thrown-away work plus a constant to unpick later. Accessory day: LiftKind stays exactly three members matching real meet structure; accessory day pays Training IQ, the §2 currency that already exists for it, and nothing lift-specific — no bestE1rmKg write, no e1RM close-out.
blockers.consequence: §3.4 now carries the coupling as a stated requirement on the module that will own it, so it cannot be lost, and §11 records it as deferred-by-decision rather than left open — with the note that the loop growth curve is not a shipping progression model and must not be tuned as one. §3.2 carries the accessory boundary, enforced in code rather than by convention. The S1 builder was redirected mid-flight: pacing fix cancelled, scope now the blind-check fixes plus the accessory boundary, with tests pinning ACTUAL behaviour and pointing at §3.4 so the gap stays visible in the suite. The V1 wiring builder was told the close-out now has three honest states rather than two — confirmed, projected, and no e1RM at all.

blockers.title: Sixteen blind checks, and the pattern held to the end
blockers.body: Every one measured a proxy rather than the claim: a generator that never produced the failing case, a bound the unfixed behaviour already satisfied, a hash standing in for a picture, a max over a region that included pixels the player cannot see, a ratio cap that a WORSE artifact satisfied more easily. Six were caught only by mutation testing.
blockers.consequence: Mutation testing is now the default ask on every dispatch, and builders have started pre-empting it unprompted — one added a source scan because it worked out that unbranding a signature would be invisible to vitest. The harness itself is now in scope: evidence bundles stamp their commit and refuse to be graded stale, and the progress page says so when a named screenshot is missing.

blockers.title: Two agents died silently, and node_modules was found wiped
blockers.body: THIRD REWIND, AND THIS ONE COST A ROUND. The working checkout silently reset to a commit from the previous day (8cd4f1c, netlify.toml) while origin held everything through wave 21. I dispatched a §8.3E builder from that rewound state, so its git worktree inherited it, and its brief described an entitlement engine that was not in the tree it could see. IT VERIFIED EVERY PREMISE BY COMMAND AND REFUSED TO BUILD - a table of eight false claims, each checked - which is exactly right and saved a round of work built on sand. Origin was intact; reset restored 2547 green. THE RULE THIS MAKES STANDING: verify HEAD before dispatching any builder, not just before reading a tracked file. A worktree inherits the main checkout state, so a rewind propagates silently into every agent spawned during it. Two earlier builders reported the same symptom from the other side, seeing an Epley-or-Brzycki CLAUDE.md and Reanimated 3 in their worktrees, and I filed both as harmless staleness rather than as the same fault. || The result-card and shot-verifier agents both last committed three days ago and never notified — the same silent kill as the earlier spend-limit halt. Four commits of finished result-card work sat unmerged the whole time. Separately, node_modules/.bin was empty and the vitest package was gone, so the suite exited 216 with NO output at all, which reads like a code crash rather than a broken install.
blockers.consequence: Both recovered by hand: npm install restored the toolchain, 21 merged worktrees were pruned to free 2.2G, and the card work is merged at 1244 tests across 23 files. The lesson is that a silent agent death looks identical to a slow one, so unmerged branches need checking by commit age rather than waiting for a notification.

blockers.title: The app is playable, and the harness that proved it was itself blind
blockers.body: App.tsx imports LiftScreen and a rep can be played in the browser — the day-one Skia spike is gone. But the tool built to prove the lift animates heavier never decoded a pixel: it hashed file bytes and compared probe values produced by the code under test. Copying the light screenshots over the maximal ones, with both manifests untouched, still made it report that the maximal attempt animates heavier. A renderer that drew nothing would have passed it.
blockers.consequence: That is the twelfth check this run that could not fail if the thing it named were deleted, and the worst, because everything downstream trusted it — including a status report I had already given. The heavier-at-maximal claim now rests on a critic's own inspection of the crops, which is a different and real basis: bar bend 3 against 1, strain climbing 0 to 3 against flat 0, ascent 69 ticks against 38. A builder is making the tool decode pixels and adding mutants that freeze the sprite while leaving the bar-path trace live.

blockers.title: Both open design questions decided by the human
blockers.body: Attempt weight: the GDD's "drop down" option is removed — within a lift, attempts repeat or increase, never decrease, and the tension is rewritten accordingly. e1RM: Epley named specifically, one formula, Brzycki banned from the codebase.
blockers.consequence: The meet engine already enforced non-decreasing, so that decision cost no code. The Epley decision did: Brzycki was the fallback past the chart's coverage precisely because Epley steps DOWN there (chart 1.7422w at rep max 16 vs Epley 1.5500w at 16.5). Rather than ship a non-monotonic curve or keep a banned formula, the module now refuses past a 16 effective rep max — a real capability loss, spelled out in its header and enumerated in tests.

blockers.title: Run halted once on the subagent spend limit, now resumed
blockers.body: Six agents were killed mid-flight when the monthly limit was hit: two critics, the e1RM rework, and the fatigue, streak and sprite builders. No usable work was lost — neither partially-started builder had committed anything, and their worktrees were discarded.
blockers.consequence: Dispatch is working again. The queue resumed in priority order: close the e1RM send-back first, then grade the two modules that were merged but never judged. The art and UI half of the run still has not started.

blockers.title: Reference now exists for some bars; four of the five still have no artifact
blockers.body: Five reference files are committed. That unblocks the sprite craft bar, which is being graded against a native-resolution SNES sprite for the first time — every earlier pass reported it unverifiable.
blockers.consequence: The other four previously-unverifiable bars cannot be re-run: the result card, gym art, meet-day sequence and cut-ins are not built yet, so there is nothing to compare. Their references are staged. Two limits remain even then — the meet photos are stills, so meet-day tension's "judge pacing and sound" half stays unverifiable without video, and the scoresheet is a live in-meet attempt board rather than a published federation results sheet.

pieces.name: Foundation
pieces.bar: Not a GDD bar — infrastructure. Must render, screenshot, and test.
pieces.note: Expo + TS strict + vitest + Skia-on-web + Playwright screenshot harness all verified working end to end.

pieces.name: RPE → %1RM table
pieces.bar: Published RPE charts. Binary and testable — critic verifies against source values.
pieces.note: WINS ITS BAR after six rounds. The final critic re-fetched both sources live at the pinned SHAs and confirmed every sampled cell matches the bytes, that the one documented disagreement is real and exactly where the module says it is, that no export remains mutable, that no indexed read can leak undefined past a null check, and that the hot path is unchanged. It named two stale-prose residuals and explicitly said not to spawn a round for them — folded into this touch instead. The chart still cannot be checked against the RTS publication from here, and the module claims no more than that.

pieces.name: e1RM formulas
pieces.bar: Published e1RM formulas. Binary and testable.
pieces.note: THE MATH WINS ITS BAR. The critic verified the Epley divisor against published sources and a pinned third-party implementation, re-fetched both chart fixtures and confirmed every cell the boundary figures depend on, hand-checked all five worked examples and the crossover point, confirmed the curve is strictly increasing across the whole domain and that the refusal fires exactly where the chart’s coverage ends, and found no invented value anywhere. All seven §12.3 conditions clean. Its one finding was a false quotation of CLAUDE.md in the module header — correct that the quote was false, but wrong about how: git history shows the phrase WAS in CLAUDE.md when the builder quoted it, and I removed it two commits later without updating the quotation. My staleness, not a fabrication. Fixed by quoting the rule as it now stands, verified verbatim against the flattened file.

pieces.name: DOTS scoring
pieces.bar: Published DOTS coefficients. Binary and testable.
pieces.note: MERGED. Every DOTS value used to be asserted against ITSELF, so a digit transposed at authoring time gave a self-consistent wrong answer with a green suite; the critic had caught the current coefficients by going outside the repo BY HAND and nothing made the next reader do that. Now 26 committed rows verified against three external implementations the builder FETCHED AND RAN locally rather than transcribed, with all ten coefficients mutation-tested one at a time: 10/10 caught at 1e-12 relative. Three of my brief claims falsified by measurement and all reported: there are NO turning points inside the domain to sample near (the real roots sit at ~228.8kg and ~153.6kg, outside the clamps, which looks like why the clamps are where they are); 2-dp published tables CANNOT support the required sensitivity, because at 0.005 seven of the ten last-digit mutations are invisible; and single transposed digit spans six orders of magnitude and is not one claim. It also found a pre-existing overstatement in the dots.test.ts header - the Python reference it credited was fed the same ten in-repo numbers, so it proved term order and not provenance. Limit recorded rather than glossed: no published TABLE of scores is reachable from this sandbox, so the fixture is the output of external code, and two of the three sources declare descent from the same crate.

pieces.name: Meet engine
pieces.bar: Meet structure correctness: order, 3 attempts, non-decreasing weight, best-per-lift total, bomb-out.
pieces.note: Structure WINS ITS BAR. Rework 5 merged: the rules-seal subsystem is gone — four constants, a unique-symbol brand, an error code, an exported check, four call sites, a 41-line essay and nine tests, including the BigInt re-derivation blind to the digits it was meant to check. Rules are now opaque behind a module-private symbol, so the tampering spread does not type-check, and the guard is proven by negative controls that revert it and confirm the directives go unused. meet.ts is 51 lines shorter and has no arithmetic left to get wrong.

pieces.name: Fatigue / readiness
pieces.bar: Plausible game-feel abstraction. No visible fatigue meter (§12.3).
pieces.note: PASSES ITS BAR. The critic had cleared the model and both live §12.3 refusal conditions, re-deriving the daily-vs-intermittent injury comparison by hand rather than taking the claim; what it sent back was two tests that could not fail if the behaviour they named were deleted. Both are now fixed and I re-ran the mutations myself rather than accepting the report: delete the technique-relief term and 1 test fails where 0 did before; delete physio shortening and 2 fail where 0 did. The technique test now pins the exact scaling across six ratings instead of asserting probability > 0, and physio is compared against the same duration roll unaided instead of restating a band the unaided value already satisfied. The third, weaker case was given real content rather than deleted, and the builder proved that by mutation too. Model untouched throughout.

pieces.name: Streak / Recovery Days
pieces.bar: Never punishes daily engagement. Manual token use, hold cap, first-break tutorial.
pieces.note: THE RULING LANDED AND THE INVARIANT HOLDS; THE RESIDUE DOES NOT. Arm-ahead is built: protection is armed by the session before an absence, the missed days consume it, and the whole offer/accept/decline surface is deleted. I verified the invariant independently — same training history across three app-opening schedules gives byte-identical results, so the outcome no longer depends on when the player looks. But the monotonicity residue SURVIVED, and the builder reported that rather than claiming the bar. I confirmed it and found the exact mechanism: trained {5,6,7} ends with balance 3 and the day-12 gap covered, streak 3; trained {0,5,6,7} ends with balance 1, the gap NOT covered, streak 0. Training day 0 opens a gap that consumes two Recovery Days which are then missing later — an extra training day converts idle days from FREE, no streak yet, into CHARGED, streak alive. So the cause recorded in §4.4 was wrong, and it was my analysis that put it there. Deleting the manual prompt was a clean test of that claim and the family did not move; Duolingo has the same property for the same reason. 36 inverting pairs over every 13-day calendar on currentStreak, worst deficit 3; the permanent record is nearly monotone at 5 pairs and deficit 1. The one change that would close it is Recovery Days ceasing to be consumed, which is a monetisation decision touching the hold cap, the earning table and §8.2 — correctly not built by a builder. || MEASURED MYSELF THIS WAVE, and the decision is now between two options rather than one. I ran an exhaustive probe: 400 seeded 40-day schedules, every single-day superset of each. At today's balance the violation count is 58 and the WORST DEFICIT IS 16 - a schedule that ends on an 18-day streak drops to 2 when one more day is trained. The named pair reproduces exactly: {5,6,7} ends on 3, {0,5,6,7} ends on 0. I then measured the proposed fix rather than assuming it: with Recovery Days never debited (coverage unchanged, balance simply not spent), the same probe returns ZERO violations, and {0,5,6,7} ends on 4 against {5,6,7} on 3 - training more now ends strictly better, which is the shape the rule wants. So option (a) is verified to close it, not hoped to. The symmetric alternative - charge the idle days BEFORE a run starts too, so the free-lunch asymmetry disappears from the other side - turns out not to be implementable without a new signup-day field on StreakState, which is a server-authoritative state-shape change; worth knowing before it is offered as the cheap option, because it is not. || RULED BY THE HUMAN, WAVE 13: option 2 — add a signup-day field and CHARGE BOTH SIDES, so the free-lunch asymmetry disappears without Recovery Days ceasing to be a consumable. Fix (a) (never debit) was measured to close it and was DECLINED because it guts the §8.2 earning table and hold cap. Signup-day is defined as ACCOUNT CREATION — the first day the player could possibly have a gap at all — and the human required that definition be stated explicitly in the module rather than left implicit. Three conditions attached to calling it done: re-run the SAME sweep that measured (a) (400+ seeded 40-day schedules plus every single-day superset) against the new implementation and confirm violations reach 0, specifically re-verifying the 18-drops-to-2 worst case; confirm the new field does not disturb the byte-identical purity invariant; and document the state field and the corrected rule in GDD §4.2 and CLAUDE.md. Builder out. It is also correcting §4.4, which still records MY WRONG CAUSE for this defect — it blames the manual Recovery-Day prompt, and deleting that prompt was run as a clean test of the claim and the defect family did not move. || WAVE 15, AND THE BUILDER CHANGED THE RULING. Two findings. FIRST, MY OWN HEADLINE NUMBER DID NOT REPRODUCE: I reported 58 violating schedules with worst deficit 16 and never pinned the seeds, so it was not reproducible. Across six natural parameterisations the builder measured 30-48 violating schedules and worst deficits 10-16, and could not find the 18-drops-to-2 pair at all - the largest it found was 23-drops-to-1. The DEFECT is real and confirmed: the named minimal pair reproduced exactly, and so did the committed 13-day pins (36 pairs / deficit 3, and 384 / 5 at 15 days). My figure was under-specified, not the code. SECOND, THE RULING AS WRITTEN CLOSES ABOUT A TENTH OF IT: signup-day alone takes 13-day violations 36 to 32 and the 40-day seed 100 to 92 pairs. The real mechanism is broader than the one I recorded. ANY free absence is a hole, because adding a trained day always splits one absence into two and splitting can only REDUCE total charge - unless a piece was free, in which case it CREATES charge from nothing. Two free cases: (a) absences before a run exists, which the human ruled on, and (b) absences that outran what was armed, which nobody had ruled on. Charging (b) alone gives 24; both give 0. The builder shipped both and flagged the second as beyond its remit rather than burying it. HUMAN RULED AGAIN: take both. A doomed absence now consumes the Recovery Days armed against it, reversing nothing is ever spent on an absence that ends the run - it punishes absence rather than engagement, so a player who shows up daily never triggers it. Three additions required before merge: commit the sweep INPUTS (seed set and attendance-generation logic) as a repo fixture so the zero-violation result is reproducible from the repository alone rather than from a conversation; enforce reported-never-silent with an explicit test over BOTH consumption events instead of describing it; and document both free-absence cases in GDD §4.2 as a rule with its own player-visible cost rather than as a footnote to the signup field. Purity invariant verified UNCHANGED: full JSON-state equality across five opening schedules over all 2^13 calendars, with two changes made specifically to preserve it. || MERGED. Exhaustive over EVERY calendar of length 8-16: violating pairs 0 at every length, against 2/10/36/124/384/1096 before, and lifetime-best inversions 0 against 1/5/19/66/211. The sweep INPUTS are a committed pure module now rather than a number in a conversation - and the distribution turned out to be the load-bearing part I had failed to record: drawing the attendance rate once per SCHEDULE rather than per DAY gives 14% of lifters below 0.3 density against 0.0%, and the long absences this property is about live in exactly that tail. A per-day draw sweeps 2000 near-identical average lifters and reports a clean zero that means nothing. Reported-never-silent is a PROPERTY now over ~294k sessions, not two examples, and building it found a real hole: the no-active-streak opening reported nothing, so a lifter about to lose the signup grant had no read model that could warn them. The builder corrected itself twice - its own event discriminator keyed on a field that SETTLING NULLS, so every dead-run loss was filed as a signup-grant expiry and the counter meant to prove the second event existed read exactly 0; and its distribution check used min/max spread, which cannot separate the two designs at all. It also corrected a figure from its own previous report. RESIDUAL, STATED RATHER THAN GLOSSED: at 60 days, 122 pairs across five seeds survive with worst deficits 9-14, attributed to milestone-income TIMING on a counterfactual that returns 0 at both lengths and all seeds - but not traced day-by-day the way the 40-day case was. Builder out on it. || TRACED, AND RULE 2 IS THE CAUSE. My explanation to the human was wrong in BOTH halves and the builder measured it: the Recovery Day is CONFISCATED, not spent - a save buys a run, a confiscation buys nothing - and it is NOT milestone timing. Income paid on FIXED CALENDAR DAYS, arriving identically for both lifters, still gives 81 violating pairs at 60 days; a balance topped to the hold cap daily so stock can NEVER run out gives 194, MORE than the shipped 122. The published counterfactual only ever showed income was INVOLVED, because milestone income is the only income the sweep has. What it actually is: the doomed branch debits the WHOLE ARMED HOLDING, so the debit is INCREASING IN WEALTH, and training more is a way of being wealthy at the wrong moment. Traced day by day, plus a second instance with no milestone involved at all. A 23-day hand-built reproduction is pinned: one extra trained day turns a final streak of 8 into 1. All three human conditions enforced BY TESTS with a mutation proving each bites. THE HEADLINE: funding a covered day with a currency TRAINING EARNS does not merely worsen the property, IT CREATES THE VIOLATIONS OUTRIGHT. CONDITIONS 1 AND 3 VERSUS THE PAY-TO-WIN ARGUMENT RESOLVED RATHER THAN PAPERED OVER: the old rule constrains the SPEND path and the provenance sits on the CREDIT path, and for the shipped expiring product the split is PROVABLY UNOBSERVABLE - (b,p) and (b+p,0) behave identically forever, proved over every split of every sum - so all three hold at once. FOUR CONTRADICTIONS INCLUDING THE GDD OWN TEXT: a bankable purchased day is NOT monotone-safe simpliciter, that was measured against zero purchases and it violates exactly where expiring violates; its own first cut let drive() grow a purchase while the battery pin did not, the exact defect §4.2 records as item 3 arriving through a new door; and a LIVE LATENT BUG the purchases exposed - the protection-declined sweep was reading a snapshot stale at a window boundary, invisible while nothing could put a number in the field. AWAITING THE HUMAN: it narrowed GDD §8.2 Chalk earning row by dropping the achievement trickle, which is a monetisation decision taken on a measurement. || HUMAN REJECTED THE SHIPPED FIX AS TOO BROAD. Removing Chalk achievement trickle globally is not the answer; the restriction belongs on the MECHANISM, not the currency. Six-part ruling: restore the achievement row to §8.2; scope §8.3E to accept only NON-TRAINING-GATED funding (calendar-earned Chalk, direct real-money purchase, or equivalent) while achievement- and tier-earned Chalk stay fully valid for cosmetics, timer skips and everything else; close the season-pass loophole EXPLICITLY rather than only the direct achievement path, because a tier every N sessions is the same shape as an achievement every N sessions; broaden the CLAUDE.md rule to say indirect paths count, since the gap existed precisely because the rule as enforced caught only DIRECT grants and not LAUNDERED ones; re-run the full sweep confirming zero across all funding sources and horizons, with the bar being that training-funded currency is STRUCTURALLY UNABLE to reach the purchase rather than empirically clean at the horizons already swept; fix AND TEST the stale-snapshot bug the purchases exposed, because finding it is not sufficient; and correct the GDD claim that a bankable purchased day is monotone-safe, which was only ever measured at zero purchases - either mark it explicitly unverified or remove it. I made the CLAUDE.md edit; a builder is out on the code. The structural bar is the interesting half: the illegal state should be unrepresentable, so a training-funded tender FAILS TO TYPECHECK and the runtime refusal is a second line rather than the only one - a clean sweep is necessary and not sufficient, being the same empirically-clean-at-the-lengths-we-tested that hid this defect twice already. || ALL SIX PARTS DELIVERED, 2586 GREEN. AND IT FALSIFIED ITS OWN STRUCTURAL CLAIM BY MUTATING IT: its first check required the responsive and frozen verdicts to agree bit for bit and it claimed in both the test AND the GDD that this caught training-sensitivity before it became a violation - but a mutation giving a legal tender one extra Chalk on the lifter 60th session MOVED 2362 OF 34338 PURCHASE-DAY LISTS at 100 days, produced zero violations, and left every aggregate identical. Sweep green, verdict green, claim false. That distinction is now in CLAUDE.md: structurally unable has two readings, the purchase cannot be constructed (a type) and the purchase day cannot move with training (not a type), and the rule means both. Two brief expectations contradicted and both right: StreakStateWire needed no change because a settled order never crosses the wire, and chalk is no longer a tender at all, which is a breaking change to a shipped signature. || SENT BACK, AND THE FINDING IS A HARD-CONSTRAINT BREACH IN ITS PLAINEST FORM. A settled covered-day purchase applied DURING an absence retroactively rescues a run openDay has already reported as streak-broken - and which way it goes depends entirely on whether anything called settleBrokenStreak first. Same calendar, same money, same day: buy-then-settle ends on 11, settle-then-buy ends on 1 with the purchase consumed for nothing. A client that settles on launch, or a nightly job, punishes the player who opens the app relative to the one who ignored it. applySettledCoveredDayPurchase writes entitlement straight onto live state with no gate on an absence in progress, and absenceOutcome resolves against state.entitlement LIVE. It contradicts a RULING - GDD §4.2 already says a Recovery Day arriving during an absence does not cover it - so this is a bug and not an open question. FOUR PLACES ASSERT THE OPPOSITE of what the code does, including settleBrokenStreak own docstring claiming it CANNOT CHANGE ANY OUTCOME while the same docstring invites a nightly job to be the thing that runs first. WHY NOTHING REDDENS is the part that matters: every harness in the repo hardcodes the safe intra-day order, and the app-opening purity test aimed at exactly this hazard - whose own comment says a covered day arriving during an absence must not rescue it - varies only WHICH DAYS the app is opened, never the ORDER WITHIN A DAY. It is green for a reason unrelated to the property it names. SECOND RESIDUAL, nearly as sharp: the exhaustive sweep NEVER CROSSES A WINDOW BOUNDARY. Lengths are 8-16, WINDOW_DAYS is 30, signupDay is anchored at 0 - so the only proof-grade sweep in the repository runs entirely inside window 0 and cannot see the refill, the re-convergence at a boundary, or a purchased day expiring. It proves the property for the sub-mechanism that was never in doubt, not the one Option 1 added. The critic also confirmed the GDD states the pooled-balance limit ACCURATELY and does not overstate it. || FIXED AND MERGED, 2592 GREEN. StreakState gains armedEntitlement - the snapshot an absence resolves against, written only by recordTrainingDay and createStreakState - while entitlement stays the live balance a purchase raises. The 11-versus-1 scenario is a committed test and reads buy-then-settle: expected 11 to be 1 when the fix is mutated away. TWO CLAIMS OF MY BRIEF FALSIFIED BY MEASUREMENT. First, THE CRITIC PRESCRIPTION ALONE BREAKS §12.3: making the doomed burn charge the ARMED count - the natural reading of §4.2 rule 2, and what resolve-against-a-snapshot implies if applied to both halves - lets a mid-absence purchase survive the absence, so an extra trained day splits it and spends a covered day the whole absence would have taken. Measured 3 violating pairs on real-money at 40 days, 23 lifetime-best inversions on the free calendar grant, and 1 in the FROZEN control where both lifters buy on identical days, which isolates it to the rule rather than the keying. So only the COVERS decision moves; the burn stays everything-live, and that asymmetry is load-bearing rather than an oversight. Second, ITS OWN FIRST FIX WAS WRONG AND ITS OWN NEW ASSERTION FOUND IT, going red on UNMUTATED code. Mutation 2 caught nothing on its first run because the sweep did not cover it, and closing that coverage gap is what surfaced the second defect. The WINDOW_DAYS 7 exhaustive sweep is clean at 982,272 pairs per arm, 0 at every length on all four figures - and its first cut was VACUOUS, because nothing can be bought inside 16 days at the shipped price, so both arms reported byte-identical consumption. AND IT CAUGHT ITSELF FABRICATING: it published a row of plausible numbers in the GDD without measuring them, then re-derived, corrected them, and said so unprompted. That is the failure this whole method exists to catch, reported by the agent that committed it. RESIDUAL FOR A HUMAN: a covered day bought BEFORE a session on the same day is armed by it, one bought AFTER arms at the next session - both follow §4.2 literally, but the clock time of a purchase is observable. Whether the store may sell during a doomed absence at all is a ruling. || RULING BUILT, 2598 GREEN. The store refuses a doomed absence by asking THE SAME CALL recordTrainingDay branches on rather than a re-derivation that could drift. THE COPY IS KEYED ON entitlementArmed AND NOT ON THE BREAK REASON, and measurement is why: breakReasonFor is ordered hardest-constraint-first, so a nightly settle lengthens the absence and FLIPS THE REASON - two different explanations for the same money on the same calendar decided by whether a background job ran, which is 11-versus-1 in the player-facing text. Caught by mutation, not review. The false-positive sweep is an EQUIVALENCE rather than a one-directional check - result.ok === protectionHolds over 98,304 store decisions, with non-vacuity pinned EXACTLY at 12,328 sellable and 85,976 refused rather than bounded. THE GUARANTEE TAGS AUDITED THEMSELVES AND THAT IS THE FINDING: coverage is 19 of 185 claims, and mutation-testing 8 of the 19 found TWO NAMING TESTS THAT STAYED GREEN WHEN THE GUARANTEE WAS BROKEN - one exercised the calendar but never a purchase, the other started from a full window so clearing the entitlement was invisible. Both tags RESOLVED PERFECTLY. A tag that resolves is not a tag that bites, and the remaining 11 carry no evidence at all. The scoping rule keys on capitalised absolutes, so a LOWER-CASE guarantee walks past - and the fifth defect own sentence was lower-case, caught only because its paragraph opened with a capital, which is recorded as luck. TWO THINGS THE BUILDER FLAGGED AGAINST ITSELF: it WEAKENED an existing assertion, conditioning the open-day sweep spend equality on the store having made the same decision, and asked for that to be looked at hard; and STORE_VERDICT_DIVERGENCE, 1 pair in 900, where on a revival day an unsettled client is SOLD where a settled one is REFUSED. That does not reach state - every full-state equality still holds - and both halves are deliberate and pinned elsewhere, so closing it means re-deriving the coverage rule or changing another piece. AWAITING A HUMAN. || COMPLETION RE-VALIDATION MERGED, 2600 GREEN, EXCEPTION COUNT ZERO. MY BRIEF WAS WRONG ABOUT HOW, AND IT IS PINNED AS A TEST RATHER THAN FILED AS A NOTE: a single settle AT the completion day does not close the gap, because on a revival day the absence still HOLDS, so the settle records NOTHING_TO_SETTLE and the revived run walks straight through. Only walking every day from the absence anchor finds the break where it actually happened. settledStateAsOf offers each day to the REAL settleBrokenStreak and keeps the first thing it records - it holds no arithmetic about grace, windows or ceilings, so it cannot disagree with the coverage rule because it has no opinion about it. THE EXISTING 98,304-DECISION DOMAIN COULD NOT EXPRESS THE CASE AT ALL - zero stale verdicts in it, because a covered absence survives four days past the last session and a 10-day calendar anchored at signup can never reach day 30, so extending only the ASSERTIONS would have been vacuous. A sixth axis was added to the SAME sweep per the ruling: 589,824 decisions. Before, re-validation removed: store sold=true, settled absence holds=false. After: completionDivergences 0 with staleVerdicts still 1984 - the two states still disagree, the store just refuses to let that decide a sale. The open-day spend equality is UNCONDITIONAL again with no second cause, and the counter stays pinned at zero so a reopening is red rather than silent. TWO THINGS IT CAUGHT AGAINST ITSELF. It WROTE A FALSE DOCSTRING AND FOUND IT: a shortcut justified with over-400s-against-27s, where the 400s was AN INFINITE LOOP - the first draft looped until probe > today, false forever when today is not a number, which the export-surface sweep triggers by calling every export with a missing argument. Timed properly the shortcut was worth 30.9s against 31.8s and nothing at all on the full suite; removed, with the wrong measurement recorded next to the right one. And A SIXTH INSTANCE of the guarantee defect, one file from where the fifth was fixed. JUDGEMENT CALL FLAGGED: the refusal COPY is keyed on this state own rendered verdict, so the sentence is not app-open invariant even though the DECISION is - the argument being that a client whose screen already said refused never produces the tap. || THE FLAGGED JUDGEMENT CALL IS BROKEN, AND THE COUNTEREXAMPLE WAS ALREADY PINNED IN THE REPO OWN TEST FILE. A fresh critic with no prior context attacked the claim that a client which rendered refused can never produce a different explanation for the same tap. ATTACK 1, one client, one device, no background job: on the last day of a window the absence is doomed and the store shows this-break-went-past-what-you-armed; ONE DAY LATER, same state object, the window turns over and coveredDaysAvailable returns a full window, so the absence is COVERED and the store legitimately offers - both ends already asserted in streak.test.ts, with the test own comment saying a rendered store screen built on this state legitimately shows the offer. The player taps and gets your-break-was-already-recorded-while-you-were-away, WHICH IS FACTUALLY FALSE: nothing recorded anything, and the screen was byte-identical to what every client and the server hold. ATTACK 2, the root cause and worse: rendered is NOT the client rendered verdict - it is absenceOutcome(state, day) where day is the COMPLETION day and state is whatever the caller passes, and SettledCoveredDayPurchase carries no rendered verdict, no render day and no idempotency key. With the module own 3am rollover, a tap at 02:50 settling at 03:10 lands on the next streak day, so a client that WAS legitimately offered the sale is told the offer should never have been on screen - the routing is exactly INVERTED. AND THE TEST THAT SHOULD HAVE CAUGHT IT CANNOT: it is a character-for-character mirror of the implementation it grades, and every probe passes the SAME day to render and completion, so the render-day-versus-completion-day axis is not in the domain at all - the hardcoded-fixture hazard one axis over from where it was last fixed. Critic verdict: BROKEN, and it ruled the no-store-UI defence invalid - a deferred hazard with a shipped justification attached is the worst combination, because the next builder reads the GDD, sees the property asserted as settled, and has no mechanism available to satisfy it. Fix builder out. || CLOSED, 2603 GREEN. Both attacks were reproduced against the unmodified tree BEFORE anything changed. The root cause was three things sharing one name: rendered was recomputed at the completion day from whatever state the caller passed, and called the client screen. Now SettledCoveredDayPurchase carries renderedOffer as an INPUT never re-derived, and one predicate is asked at two horizons. ABSENCE_SETTLED_WHILE_AWAY is deleted because it asserted a recording event the module cannot observe. WHY ~590,000 GREEN DECISIONS MISSED AN INVERTED ROUTING: the after-offer case is UNREACHABLE AT LAG 0, and every probe passed the same day to render and completion - so the sweep gains a render-day-lag axis rotated over the existing domain at no probe cost, and the mirror oracle that restated the implementation character-for-character is replaced. ITS OWN FIRST FIX WAS WRONG IN A NEW WAY: it routed on when a break was RECORDED, and a never-trained lifter never has one recorded while their signup absence still runs out on a definite day - 6 day-pairs in a fresh account first 40 days mislabelled. The oracle it wrote to catch that SHARED THE BLIND SPOT EXACTLY, independent in FORM and dependent in the FACT IT READ. That is the seventh instance of the guarantee pattern and a sub-case CLAUDE.md did not warn against; it does now. Two rulings reasoned rather than deferred: no idempotency key, because the only place to put one is StreakState which every §12.3 sweep compares byte-for-byte; and two devices are out of reach honestly, with each screen getting a sentence true of itself while the DECISION is identical. pieces.bar: Dread and anticipation comparable to a real third-attempt walkout.
pieces.note: MERGED, AND THE BUILDER REPORTED MY BRIEF WRONG. I told it to pin foreign CROWD_MID in the window non-own columns against REST_BAND as the strong form. It measured that and found it RED ON CORRECT ART: a tier own keyline is legitimately stamped over the tier behind inside its window, so the count legitimately falls as the crowd rises. It published the full 4x11 table and fell back to the one-sided form, which reads 0 at every rise for the back tier - that window exclusivity as a measurement rather than an argument. The load-bearing mutation is the one that matters: foreign CROWD_MID inside a tier OWN columns at rises 1-3, contiguous with its head. Whole tree before: 2447 green, COMPLETELY INVISIBLE. After: red. It also flagged, unprompted, that even the strong form would not have closed the named gap, because foreign paint in the own columns is disjoint from the pixels that count looks at. Fresh critic out. || WAVE 15: THE CRITIC VERIFIED THE WHOLE ROUND and confirmed the builder was right to refuse my instructions, re-deriving the keyline geometry itself and measuring net -74 against the reported 321->246. Then it found the ceiling was a BOUND where it is structurally an EQUALITY, with a comment citing a saturation case the same test forbids three lines earlier. Cost, demonstrated not argued: make paintCrowd apply rowRise only at rise>=5, so the whole interior of the 900ms walk-out ramp draws a seated hall and the crowd pops up in one step on the final frame - whole tree 2470 GREEN. With the pin: 1 failed. The builder re-derived on RENDERED PIXELS rather than prose and returned two refinements, then checked the pin does not redden on legitimate retuning. The :508 sentence did NOT become true on its own, contrary to both the critic expectation and mine. || CRITIC PASSED THE SPATIAL HALF OUTRIGHT, and re-derived it from paintCrowd itself rather than taking the file word: the pin is structurally safe INCLUDING the back tier - it checked the previously hand-waved clipping case and found the equality holds there for a DIFFERENT reason, which is what the comment says - the pin does not redden on legitimate retuning, all three ARGUED/MEASURED labels are honest, the one-sided foreign count is the CORRECT negative result because a risen tier 7-column keyline necessarily wipes the tier behind inside its own window, and the domain sweep genuinely covers negatives, fractionals and past-saturation. THEN IT FOUND THE INSTRUMENT HAS NO TIME AXIS. Nothing in the tree relates a crowd rise to WHEN in the 900ms ramp it is drawn. The test named comes-up-over-time-rather-than-switching-on maps the sheet to rise values and THROWS startMs AWAY - the entire temporal claim is a Set cardinality check plus monotonicity. WALKOUT_RISE_MS is referenced by one assertion, toBeGreaterThan(0), in the test whose own name is what-this-file-does-NOT-claim; WALKOUT_RISE_DELAY_MS by NO assertion at all. Concrete: compress the rise into the last quarter and the hall sits completely dead for 675ms of 900ms then pops up in 225ms - the beat anticipation channel replaced with a jump-scare, on the one screen §12.2 judges for dread - and the WHOLE TREE STAYS GREEN. Fourth instance of this file signature defect, and the test standing over the hole is named for it and cannot see it. || TIME AXIS BUILT, AND THE RESIDUAL PREMISE FALSIFIED. The compression left the whole tree green before and reddens two named tests after, with the message naming the instant. One correction to the critic arithmetic, measured on the quantised sheet rather than estimated: the hall sits dead for 720ms of 900 and pops up in 140, not 675/225. WHICH HALF IS LOAD-BEARING IS STATED RATHER THAN ASSUMED: the quarter pin the brief asked for CANNOT catch the compression, because both its sides read the same function - confirmed by tripling crowdRowRise and watching it stay green. The spread and stillness bounds are what close the gap. THE DOWNWARD-GROWTH RESIDUAL PREMISE WAS WRONG: the mutation it has cited three times CHANGES NO PIXEL, byte-identical at one row, three rows and twelve - two whole tier pitches - across all 22,490 pixels at every rise. The tree was green because there was nothing to see. Now pinned at zero slack and calibrated by running. It also deleted an assertion the brief implied and four it wrote itself, each after finding it could not fail for its own reason.

The test named leaves the grid, the total and the barbell exactly where they were compared ONE row — strip bottom 73 against grid header 74, so the loop ran once over a blank gutter. It now compares rows 73 to 239 inclusive, full width: 167 rows, 32064 pixels, and THAT COUNT IS ITSELF ASSERTED, which is the assertion the old one-row loop would have failed. The builder had to build the fixture rather than tweak one, and measured why nothing weaker works: at CONTENT.W 180 the masters phrase renders 217px and wraps, changing the division alone still gives 190px and still wraps, so only Raw / Open at 152px produces a genuine one-line twin. Both halves report the same total, DOTS and placing, hand-written in the test so a zero pixel diff cannot be two cards agreeing about nothing, and the attempts are retyped rather than shared with sampleCards so sample drift makes the pair disagree out loud. Six layout constants moved one at a time, all six caught. Crucially the builder noticed the diff alone could not catch them — moving a constant moves BOTH cards and the diff stays zero — so it also mutated the renderer to move the total block on the one-line card ONLY, which is the shape the A/B half exists for, and that failed correctly. It disclosed one surviving mutation rather than hiding it: spilling the second meta line out of the strip passes, because drawGrid repaints those rows afterwards, so the A/B half real coverage below row 74 is narrower than its framing suggests. It also flagged that hand-written absolute row pins mean the coming 30-iteration tuning pass will see test failures rather than screenshot differences. pieces.name: Cross-module inconsistency (found, unfixed)
pieces.bar: The four modes must feel like one game — the smoothing-pass concern.
pieces.note: ROUND 10 VERIFIED SOUND ON EVERY CLAIM - AND THE ELEVENTH STEP IS THE INTERVAL BETWEEN BORN AND ADMITTED. The critic proved assertion 1 is NOT CIRCULAR from the evidence itself: the CLI filtered the run to one file and the assertion still passed with executed.length > 50 and set equality against 20+ dropped files, so globTestSpecifications genuinely re-globs rather than echoing the invocation. Assertion 2’s edges really are TypeScript’s, covering import-equals, module specifiers including bare export-star, import() calls, import() TYPES and @/* path aliases, with the only misses a computed specifier the compiler cannot resolve either and residual 3. It also ranked the three remaining filters and found the builder’s "largest" wrong: isDeclarationFile is irreducible, IS_VENDORED does no work today, and the target names are WELL DEFENDED FROM THE OTHER SIDE, because a genuinely new fact type must add a field and that reddens 7’s derived fact-set assertions. THE GAP: all three tallied kinds are CONSTRUCTIONS OR CALLS - record and wire are born, receive is admitted - and an assignment is neither. readonly does not stop one, because READONLY IS NOT PART OF ASSIGNABILITY, so it aliases away with no cast at all. deepFreeze runs only on the minted snapshot; snapshotWireFor and newServerRecord hand out plain unfrozen objects, and two shipped sites already hold one in flight. I RAN IT: three lines at useSession.ts:276 writing a pound e1RM into response.wire give tsc CLEAN and 57 files / 2439 tests, IDENTICAL COUNTS. No literal assignable to either target, no new receiveProgressionSnapshot call (the door is entered through sessionClient.receiveSnapshot, whose callers are not pinned), no reflective idiom, no numeric literal for the auditor. That is THE BAR ITSELF failing with all four guards green. It also falsifies the table’s one unqualified claim about itself - "ONE producer, so bestE1rmKg and totalKg leave the server through a single function". One producer, yes; one WRITER, no. And it is strictly easier than every idiom on residual 1’s list: no cast, no reflection API, no any, no new identifier, one line at a site that already exists. Dispatched with FREEZE as the recommended route rather than a fourth scan, because every round of this piece has added an instrument a later round found scoped too narrowly, and freezing removes the capability instead of enumerating its uses. || THE COHERENCE PASS FAILED THE BAR, AND THE CAUSE IS ONE MISSING PROP. Meet day plays A DIFFERENT LIFTER than the one you just trained. useMeetDay calls newServerRecord on mount and builds the entire meet from it; AppShell gives SessionScreen a serverPort and gives MeetScreen NO PORT, NO RECORD, NO CACHE; and appSessionPort holds the app one server connection that useMeetDay never asks for. So in the shipped path, forever: bestE1rmKg is the signup seed, so every meet suggests the same three openers on day 1 and day 400; totalKg is null, so the recap says FIRST TOTAL every time; record.meets is empty, so isPrAttempt is permanently false and GDD §6.3 attempt tension - the thing the document itself calls THE REAL TENSION - IS DEAD CODE IN THE SHIPPED APP; and MEET_ALREADY_RECORDED, the guard against banking one meet twice, can never fire. THE REPO HAD ALREADY DIAGNOSED AND FIXED THIS EXACT DEFECT TWICE, in headers that argue the general case - it reached for the row, the connection belongs to the app not to a screen, the ternary is a full unmount - and the guard EXISTS: sessionWiring.test.ts bans six strings from useSession.ts as exactly what the bypass was made of, and useMeetDay.ts CONTAINS FIVE OF THEM plus the meet analogue of the sixth, with zero matching guards of its own. Same bypass, one hook over, guarded in one place and assumed in the other. The sharpest detail: meetServer.ts comments on meetDayFacts that it is THE ONE PLACE A TRAINING NUMBER CROSSES INTO MEET DAY and makes that number unit compile-time provable - and the crossing does not happen, so the number is unit-proven and constant. The critic also showed the only recap screenshot ever taken showing COMPETITION PR is the FROZEN DEBUG PATH fed a fabricated 605kg history: the played app cannot produce that picture. Not one of the 94 browser checks compares a quantity on the two sides of the press that crosses modes. Builder out. || FIXED AND MERGED, 2644 GREEN, 102 BROWSER CHECKS. Measured in a browser on the shipped route with no query string: before, a played session ending at bench 124.6 drew an opener of 107.5, which is 0.9 x the 120 SIGNUP SEED; after, it draws 110.0, the number the session implies. I opened the new shot and the bench opener reads 110, under copy that says Pre-filled from your training - true for the first time. THE REPRODUCTION COST TWO FINDINGS WORTH MORE THAN THE PLUMBING. The input-completeness control REFUSED TO RUN rather than passing over unreadable inputs, because the parser read STARTING_E1RM.deadlift as missing - it is the last entry of an inline object with no trailing comma. And at the harness ordinary readiness answers, A PERFECTLY PLAYED DAY-1 SESSION DOES NOT BEAT THE SIGNUP SEED on any lift at any of the five RPEs, and bestE1rmKg is monotone, so the record reads EXACTLY the seed - indistinguishable from the empty record the defect fabricates. THE EQUALITY WOULD HAVE PASSED VACUOUSLY ON THE BROKEN BUILD; only the non-vacuity control made that visible. Structurally: the port is a required first parameter, the ban forbids the row-building names, MeetServerPort exposes none, and appSessionPort() === appMeetPort(). The preview ternary that was one branch doing two jobs is replaced by the preview server and its state being ONE VALUE, so they cannot disagree. meetDayFacts now takes a structural MeetDayHistory rather than a ServerRecord - that parameter type WAS the cause, since a client may not hold a row and so had to fabricate one to have something to pass. Ten mutations; the sharpest TYPECHECKS and hands the client the whole ServerRecord under a key nobody was watching. An EIGHTH instance of the guarantee pattern found in passing: appServer.ts cited a test file that does not exist. NEWLY REACHABLE AND FLAGGED: MEET_ALREADY_RECORDED fires on the second meet of an app run - correct, not a dead end, but the recap is blank with a way out, and the entry gate belongs to GDD §6.1 Career calendar. || PLACEHOLDER SHIPPED PER THE HUMAN RULING, 2651 GREEN, 103 BROWSER CHECKS. Reproduced first on real numbers: meet 1 banks 612.5kg under local-open-2026 and its recap builds, meet 2 reports the SAME id and is refused, so the beat stayed recap with no recap object and the screen fell through to a bare MEET COMPLETE eyebrow. The scaffolding test catches: the module imports only TYPES, so a file that imports no values cannot read a clock, a row or meet history; the export surface is exact BOTH ways; the view takes no props; both files carry a code-line ceiling; and the pin runs in both directions between the module and GDD §6.1. What it CANNOT catch is stated rather than implied, and two of those limits are MEASURED - adding an optional prop to the view left tsc COMPLETELY SILENT, which is why that check is textual, and a nextMeetDay function needs no import at all and sails past the type-only bound, which is why the export-surface check is the one that actually catches scheduling. A NEW SHAPE OF THE VACUITY FAILURE, FOUND IN ITS OWN WORK: its first pin was SOURCE.includes(THE_CONSTANT) where the module declares that constant from a literal, so the file necessarily contains its own value and the assertion CANNOT FAIL - every previous instance in this codebase was prose without a test, this one is a test assertion that cannot fail, and the witness bar does not catch it because a witness proves ONE assertion bites rather than all of them. BROWSER LIMIT DISCLOSED: the positive case is NOT verified in a browser, because reaching the placeholder needs two whole meets in one page session and the rep is a genuine timing mechanic a scripted mouse does not beat reliably, so the committed check is the negative half only and the code says so. AWAITING A HUMAN: the copy says Meet recorded, and the meet just lifted was NOT recorded - it was refused, and the result on the row is the EARLIER meet. True of the row, arguably misleading about the nine attempts just taken. || COPY CORRECTED BY THE HUMAN. It now reads Meet complete - results saved to your last recorded meet. Career calendar coming soon. The old line claimed the meet was recorded when it was REFUSED, and any number the app can show belongs to the EARLIER meet - true of the row, misleading about the nine attempts just taken, and that distinction is the entire reason the screen exists. The builder shipping it unedited and flagging it rather than quietly changing it is what made the correction possible. THE SELF-REFERENTIAL ASSERTION IS FIXED AND I MUTATION-TESTED THE REPLACEMENT rather than taking the report word: removing the section citation from the module now reddens by name. AND VACUITY IS ITS OWN NAMED CATEGORY in CLAUDE.md now, separate from the prose-without-a-test rule, because they are different failure shapes needing different scans and they look identical in a green suite. The definition is stated so it can be applied - an assertion is vacuous if NO STATE of the code it is meant to be checking would make it red, not it-passes-today but there-is-no-version-of-the-subject-that-fails-it - with six shapes listed from this run own history: self-referential, an empty domain, a bound the unfixed behaviour already satisfied, an oracle mirroring its subject, a domain that cannot reach the case, and an input silently absent.

pieces.name: Sponsor / licensed-content architecture
pieces.bar: A real-IP audit finds nothing, and fictional entries exercise all three identity tiers end to end.
pieces.note: TIERS 2 AND 3 WIN OUTRIGHT; TIER 1 IS FIXED AND ITS LIMIT IS NOW A HUMAN QUESTION. The real-IP audit is default-deny on renderable strings with five plants all caught, a self-scan that fires on its own header, and a citation list pinned in BOTH directions so deleting provenance fails too. Tier 1 colorways were three-of-four INVALID - equipment-bank indices that would have classified a partner singlet as barbell to every silhouette measurement in the codebase - and the check could not see it because it validated them in a Tier 3 sheet palette. Fixed, and Tier 1 now reaches a real rendered sprite. The finding underneath is the valuable part: bank 0 holds only SINGLET, GEAR, HAIR and CHALK for kit, so a partner green or crimson CANNOT exist without spending a palette slot, and 7.3s no-change-at-all claim is true only for partners whose colours bank 0 already has. Logged for a human rather than amended. The builder also returned a qualified NO on the architecture I proposed, naming the CRAM-swap end state the remap only approximates.

pieces.name: App shell / navigation
pieces.bar: A player can reach every mode without a debug URL, and no surface is a dead end.
pieces.note: CRITIC PASSED THE PLAYER-FACING BAR on evidence it actually inspected: it opened all twelve PNGs and read route.json line by line and they AGREE. 82 checks, 0 failures, 0 page errors. The traversal is real end to end, no pill on any of the eight mechanic beats or over a cut-in, no Total and no fatigue readout in chrome, refusal conditions clean. THEN IT FOUND THE HOLE IN MY OWN HARNESS FIX, IN THE SAME FILE I HAD JUST FIXED. SELF_DIRTYING was correctly a denylist; codeChangedBetween ten lines below it was an ALLOWLIST of src/package.json/tsconfig/vitest.config - and App.tsx and index.ts are at the REPO ROOT, and so is all of tools/, INCLUDING THE INSTRUMENT THAT WRITES THE RECORD. Its demonstration, which I ran down and which holds: change App.tsx to <AppShell /> and it TYPECHECKS, because search is optional and defaults to null; every debug route then boots the daily check-in, so ~40 of route.json 82 checks describe screens the app cannot draw - and vitest green, tsc green, --verify says current and green. Now default-deny: diff everything, subtract run artefacts and prose by name. Second half of the finding: a SHA cannot distinguish a stale app from a stale INSTRUMENT - edit ON_SCREEN_MIN_OPACITY to 0 and every committed ok line is attributed to a device that no longer exists, at an unchanged commit. capturedFrom now carries sha256 digests of the tools that produced it and --verify re-hashes them. Both new checks were WATCHED FAILING before being committed. Builder out on the four residuals: the App.tsx hand-off assertion, 08-set-has-no-nav.png (which photographs the REST beat, not a set), the nav table pin being one-sided against the game (weigh-in and openers are in neither list), and a prose overclaim about every number being derived or controlled. || WAVE 15 REWORK MERGED, 82 -> 94 BROWSER CHECKS. The premise was confirmed on the base commit: <AppShell /> gave tsc EXIT 0 and left all 2457 tests green, while every debug URL and deep link silently booted DEFAULT_ROUTE. Two instruments now, because neither covers the other - search is REQUIRED so tsc catches the deletion, but search={null} still typechecks, which is exactly why the second exists: a TypeScript-AST DATA-FLOW scan that walks the repo FROM THE ROOT, finds every non-test file mounting <AppShell>, and requires some attribute of it to be fed by a .location.search read through locals or one import hop. It pins the FLOW, not the spelling: renaming the prop or extracting the read stays green; search={null} and a defined-but-unpassed helper both go red. Following package.json main needed the DYNAMIC import handled, without which App.tsx is unreachable from index.ts and the walk finds one module. The mis-named photograph is fixed by welding structure to an assertion rather than trusting structure: one shutter per beat INSIDE the loop, each requiring the screen to carry that beat own line, plus a new 08b for the rest. I opened both - 08 shows SET 1 OF 5 / TAP AND HOLD TO DESCEND with the lifter in the gym, 08b shows RACK IT / NEXT SET, neither with a pill. The nav table is now a PARTITION of the 14 declared phases. weigh-in and openers went on the TUNABLE list rather than the never-list, on the reasoning that no pill on the weigh-in is today tuning answer and not a GDD refusal, and filing them under never would smuggle a design decision nobody made into the one list the file calls unmovable - the builder judgement call, flagged, and I agree with it. The every-number-is-derived overclaim now has two real controls. 13 mutations, all watched failing. It also found that GDD §12.2 correction 3 PRESCRIBES THIS EXACT FIX SHAPE - enumerate over the project own file list with a file outside src/ named BY HAND - and that its own root anchor was only indirectly protected, so it added the hand-named anchors in a third commit.

pieces.name: Cut-in firing gate (mechanism, not art)
pieces.bar: One per session enforced by the gate itself; always skippable; fires only at 7.2 moments; Tier 3 surface path reused, not duplicated.
pieces.note: MERGED. The header no longer documents the architecture the fix deleted - and the builder scan found THREE MORE files carrying the same false claim that no critic had reported: cutInGate.ts, WalkoutView.tsx, CloseOutView.tsx. The mechanism is the keeper: a comment-only scan banning an ORDERED claim (subject, present-tense provenance verb, object) inside one sentence, with six disowning constructions blocking it, so the historical note explaining why the sentence went survives while the sentence itself cannot return. onlyComments is asserted to partition each file character-for-character against withoutComments. Falsifier, positive control and negative control all reported. Alias hole closed with the ts type checker rather than by re-answering what counts as an import textually. I then had to correct one more sentence MYSELF: its header said frames.json carries no capturedFrom, true when written and falsified by the harness work landing in parallel the same hour. Fifth instance in this file. Fresh critic out. || CRITIC SWEPT EVERY REFUSAL CONDITION CLEAN and confirmed the pixels by opening them; it reported the art bar UNVERIFIABLE because there is no 16-bit cut-in reference in the repo and it cannot display a remote image, which is the honest call. Its finding: the new comment ban scans for FIVE SPELLINGS, not for the claim. THE_PANEL does not match the bare noun panel at all. Delete two words from a real shipped sentence - the placeholder panel the licensing system already renders - and the pattern misses, the test passes, and a sentence whose meaning is fully intact is back in the header telling the next builder to rebuild the architecture §7.2 ruled against. Same one-word deletion defeats two of the other three. It also found THE_DELETED_CLAIMS is simultaneously the corpus the regex was fitted to AND the only proof it works - the self-agreement this same file refuses elsewhere. Builder out on that plus four more: a false causal claim about DISMISS_ENABLED_AFTER_MS (nothing outside its own test calls the function that reads it), an existsSync pin that passes for untracked files, a false every number claim, and the name-laundering half of the alias hole. || MERGED. The old ban was five spellings of one noun, and the builder reproduced every escape VERBATIM before changing anything: the two-word deletion escaped, so did the same deletion from a second real sentence, so did a full-stop split, so did every verb outside the list of eleven. Only one of the four shipped sentences was caught, and only because it independently spells a filename. Rewritten as subject + object within a bounded gap with the VERB LIST DELETED and past tense demoted to a disowner. Held-out test written after the pattern was frozen and run once: EIGHT OF TWELVE, with the four misses pinned AS MISSES rather than tuned away - and one of them is a refusal with evidence, because the reversed-order form would redden six true sentences including two about the meet JUDGING panel, a homonym. The new ban immediately caught five sentences in the header the builder had just written. It also found the partition assertion is not merely tautological but FALSE: checked against the TypeScript parser, onlyComments loses 58 characters of a real comment out of BOTH halves, so the property the old test claimed does not hold on this repository own files - and the prose ban runs on that stream. Then that new check fired on N1 work the moment the two merged, finding a SECOND instance, 37 characters, in a file written in parallel. Recorded rather than dodged: the one-line fix is to reword the comment, and rewording prose to avoid a scanner defect is how a defect stops being visible without stopping being real. || CRITIC SWEPT EVERY REFUSAL CONDITION CLEAN, confirmed by reading the code path that the dismiss window is genuinely on the tap route now, and confirmed from the committed pixels that the §7.2 ruling holds on screen. Art bar reported UNVERIFIABLE - no 16-bit cut-in reference exists in the repo. Its finding: THE BAN OWN TWO KNOBS ARE PINNED BY NOTHING, and every fixture in the file avoids the axis they control. It measured them by hand: max subject-to-object gap is 20 chars across the historical claims, 27 across the escapes, 47 across the held-outs, and the pronoun fixture antecedent distance is 6 - against CLAIM_GAP 60 and PRONOUN_REACH 160. So both could be lowered, WEAKENING the ban, and every test stays green. Nothing distinguishes 48 from 60 from 600. Concrete escape, and NOT adversarial: one edit to a sentence that genuinely shipped in this file puts the subject 88 characters from the object and it is defeated purely BY LENGTH - and this codebase prose register is nothing but long qualified clauses, so the escape is the house style. Same species this piece was sent back for twice, now living INSIDE the guard built to stop that species, in the same round that fixed the second instance. It also found EXIT_MS is the THIRD instance: documented as how long it takes to leave, read only by a helper whose only callers are three unit assertions, and the committed pixels disprove it - tapDismissed records goneAt 12ms after tappedAt against a claimed 100. Setting it to 0 leaves the suite green and moves no pixel. || BOUNDS PINNED, AND WIDENING WAS IMPOSSIBLE. Both knobs are now straddled - a caught positive at the value, a declared miss one past it - so moving either in either direction reddens a named test. Eighteen mutations. Three corrections, two to the critic: PRONOUN_REACH could NOT be lowered to 6, the measured floor is 15 and the critic measured one fixture and missed another; and the values could not be RAISED AT ALL, because once tools/ is in scope the corpus ceiling is 65 while the escape needs 90 - so widening was impossible rather than risky, and the fix had to be structural. Corpus MINED rather than invented: 191 files, ~18,000 sentences, 171 carrying a panel token - and it reports the limit honestly, that RECALL CANNOT BE MEASURED on the real corpus because the corpus contains zero true positives, the tree being clean being the entire point. EXIT_MS deleted rather than wired: wiring it would have added an unplayed beat GDD §7.2 does not ask for and left a full-screen Pressable over the screen for 100ms after the tap. The deletion is enforced by the type checker.

groups.title: MVP — one loop playable end to end on a device — MET
groups.body: MET as of this commit, and verified on the running app rather than asserted. A player opens the app, does a daily session, enters a meet, completes it and comes back, without typing a URL: 47 of 47 checks pass, including PRESSING IT REACHES MEET DAY with no query string and FINISH A SESSION to REACH A MEET in one press. The estimate was 1 build plus 1 to 2 reworks at high confidence; it took 1 build and 0 reworks, which is the fastest any piece has landed in this run. Two caveats stated rather than buried: 6.1 Career gating is not built, so there is one ungated door to one local meet; and the already-trained-today surface is unit-tested but has no rendered frame, which is the one place the never-punish argument would want pixels.

groups.title: Alpha — four modes present, math and rules bars won
groups.body: The math half is effectively there: five of six lifting-math and rules pieces have won. The mode half is not — three of the four modes are zero files. Estimate: roughly 12 to 18 rounds. Basis, from this run: a piece from nothing to a won bar has cost 4 to 6 rounds (M1 six, M4 five, S2 five so far, A1 five and still unmet), and three unbuilt modes plus cut-ins is four pieces. MEDIUM CONFIDENCE on the arithmetic, LOW on the total, because every mode built so far surfaced gaps in pieces that were already called done — the S2 venue work broke A2 palette assumptions, and A1 shading broke A2 negative controls.

groups.title: Beta — art bars won where gradeable, tuning set by playtesting
groups.body: NOT REACHABLE FROM INSIDE THIS RUN, and that is a fact about the environment rather than an estimate. GDD §12.1 budgets roughly 30 hand-tuning iterations by actual playtesting, and every walkout duration, judging threshold, crowd rise, haptic pattern and sound recipe is currently an unplayed placeholder that says so in its own header. No critic can substitute for that — CLAUDE.md is explicit. The rounds I can still spend usefully are the ones that make values tunable and honest, not the ones that set them.

groups.title: Permanently unverifiable here, and why
groups.body: Three bars cannot be settled in this environment no matter how many rounds are spent. The 16-bit era A/B for gym art: docs/reference/README.md records that no gym-interior reference is committed, and image hosts return 403 by policy. Meet-day pacing and sound: broadcast footage is unreachable, WebFetch returns markdown rather than pixels or audio, and nothing here can capture sound. Result-card typography: four separate critics confirmed the 403s themselves rather than inheriting the claim. In each case the honest outcome is the one taken — the artifact is built to be tunable and the bar is reported unverifiable rather than passed on argument.

groups.title: What the count means, and why it will grow again
groups.body: Seven of twenty-two is the strict reading: won means a critic passed it with no open gap. Six more (M2, M3, M4, A2 and others above) are majority-passes where everything gradeable was met and the residue is either awaiting a human ruling or is permanently unverifiable. The denominator is pieces DEFINED SO FAR and has grown twice: the licensing architecture did not exist as a piece two days ago, the app shell was invisible until this recount, and cut-ins have had a GDD bar all along with nobody assigned. Twenty-four checks that could not fail have been found so far, and each new piece has surfaced more; the realistic expectation is that Y keeps rising as the remaining modes expose gaps in pieces currently called done.
